evals.prompt: Write a provider for an Anthropic-style API that reads rate limits from response headers, so adaptive-rate-limiter can track them.
evals.expected_output: A class subclassing ProviderInterface implementing all four abstract members.
expectations: Implements all four members: name, discover_limits, parse_rate_limit_response, get_bucket_for_model
parse_rate_limit_response returns a RateLimitInfo and sets is_rate_limited when status_code is 429

evals.prompt: My API has no endpoint to list rate limits up front — limits only appear in response headers. What should discover_limits return in my adaptive-rate-limiter provider?
evals.expected_output: Explains discover_limits should return an empty dict when discovery is unsupported.
expectations: States discover_limits should return an empty dict when discovery is unsupported
States discover_limits should not raise an exception in that case

evals.prompt: How do I implement get_bucket_for_model in my adaptive-rate-limiter provider when some models I don't recognize?
evals.expected_output: Implements get_bucket_for_model and explains returning model_id as a fallback.
expectations: Implements get_bucket_for_model as an async method returning a string
Explains that returning model_id itself is a safe fallback for unknown models

evals.prompt: In my adaptive-rate-limiter provider the upstream API only sometimes sends the `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` header. When that header is missing, what should parse_rate_limit_response put in RateLimitInfo.tpm_remaining — should I carry forward the last known value or derive it from the limit?
evals.expected_output: Says missing rate-limit fields must be left as None, never estimated or carried forward.
expectations: States that when a rate-limit header is absent the corresponding RateLimitInfo field must be left as None
States the provider must not estimate, carry forward, or otherwise guess missing rate-limit values

evals.prompt: I'm writing a custom provider and want discover_limits to return the same bucket type the scheduler uses internally. I found `RateLimitBucket` in adaptive_rate_limiter/types. Should discover_limits return dict[str, RateLimitBucket]?
evals.expected_output: Says to use DiscoveredBucket, not the internal RateLimitBucket type.
expectations: States that discover_limits must return DiscoveredBucket objects (dict[str, DiscoveredBucket]), not RateLimitBucket
Notes that RateLimitBucket and the internal types module are not part of the public API and should not be relied on

evals.prompt: My custom adaptive-rate-limiter provider's discover_limits() calls an upstream API that intermittently returns HTTP 503. When that happens I want to raise an exception. Is BackendConnectionError the right one to raise, or is there a provider-specific exception?
evals.expected_output: Recommends raising ProviderError (from adaptive_rate_limiter) for provider-side failures, not BackendConnectionError.
expectations: Recommends raising ProviderError (importable from adaptive_rate_limiter) when a provider method fails, such as an upstream discovery API returning 503
States that BackendConnectionError is not appropriate here because it is for storage-backend (Redis/memory) failures, not provider failures
Shows how to raise ProviderError from within a provider method, e.g. checking the upstream response status and raising on a 503
